text: kb-rag 是面向 DSH 桌面端的本地文献知识库插件。它注册十个知识库工具，并提供会话控制命令和浏览器侧来源卡片；引擎将 PDF、TXT、Markdown、DOCX 与 Zotero 附件切分、索引到本地 SQLite，再以关键词和向量混合检索返回带章节、页码、DOI 与引文信息的证据。主要功能包括批量入库、深度检索与引文问答、DOI 或 arXiv PDF 获取，以及可选 HTML 答案页。适合需要管理论文资料并追溯回答来源的研究者。无需模型 API Key；首次使用需准备 Python 依赖并下载本地模型。

kb-rag is a DSH desktop plugin for a local paper library. It ingests PDFs and Zotero attachments into SQLite, then returns cited passages through keyword and vector search. It supports evidence based answers, DOI or arXiv PDF lookup, and HTML reports. Python dependencies and local models are needed.
我想把一整个论文文件夹建成本地知识库，之后可以直接提问。
能不能从 Zotero 里把带 PDF 的文献批量导进来？
我需要搜论文段落，并看到它来自哪篇文章、哪一页。
帮我根据自己的文献库回答问题，还要给出可追溯的引用。
我有 DOI 或 arXiv 编号，想找 PDF 并补进我的资料库。
我想把检索结果整理成一页可以保存和分享的 HTML 报告。
I want to search my paper library with both keywords and semantic similarity.
Can I migrate my Zotero PDFs into a local searchable library and track citations?
kb-rag 的功能「文献入库」：导入 PDF、TXT、Markdown 或 DOCX 文件和目录，按章节提取元数据并写入本地库；内容未变化的文件可跳过，大批量任务可返回后台 job_id 供轮询。
kb-rag 的功能「Zotero 迁移」：读取本机 Zotero 数据库和 PDF 附件，把文献元数据及附件导入知识库；可先 dry_run 预览候选，也可限制迁移数量。
kb-rag 的功能「混合检索」：对知识库片段结合关键词 BM25 与向量召回，并按元数据过滤；quick 快速返回，deep 可启用精排和关联文献。
kb-rag 的功能「证据问答」：检索相关文献片段并整理为 evidence，提示模型按证据作答；深度模式还可附带引文链与相关文献。
kb-rag 的功能「论文 PDF 获取」：提交 DOI 或 arXiv 编号，按出版商页面和开放获取来源寻找 PDF，下载后放入本地目录并记录 manifest。
kb-rag 的功能「HTML 答案页」：在 RAG 调用中提供 answer 规格时，引擎会把证据与答案字段渲染成可保存的 HTML 文件，并返回文件结果。
kb-rag 的功能「会话检索设置」：用 kb_scope 或 /kb 命令切换库内或联网范围、quick/deep 深度、严格模式和答案格式，并可保存工作区默认设置。
kb-rag 的功能「知识库维护」：查看文档与向量统计、轮询后台入库状态、去除重复文档，或通过显式确认清空知识库。
kb-rag 使用本地 embedding 与 reranker 模型；首次调用需要下载模型文件并在本机准备 Python 依赖。
DSH 与 MCP 服务默认使用不同的知识库目录：DSH 采用工作区 .kb，MCP 默认使用 ~/.kb-rag；需要共享资料时应显式指定 kb_root。

dsh-kb-rag README · What 1.6.8 changes：1.6.8 fixes two things that broke the DSH 0.2 install: the peer range and the client injection list. With both wrong, the plugin was rejected during install and the tool cards stayed empty.

dsh-kb-rag README · What 1.6.8 changes：The release also adds HTML answer pages rendered by the engine and a title-level probe. `kb_stats` now reports model cache state, and deep searches return `no_hit` when the best reranked score stays below the floor. The search core is otherwise unchanged: on the same library, results line up with 1.6.7. The full list is in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md).
dsh-kb-rag README · Install：kb-rag runs in the DSH desktop app. Install it from the plugin panel. The command-line routes exist for maintainers and old web deployments; new users do not need them.

dsh-kb-rag README · A. DSH desktop app：1. Open **Settings → Plugins** (设置 → 插件).
2. Search `kb-rag`. The package is `dsh-kb-rag`, and the entry should say **1.6.8**.
3. Install, restart DSH, and start a new conversation.

The desktop app needs to be 0.2 or newer. 1.6.7 and earlier fail that version's compatibility check; 1.6.8 is the first release that passes it.

dsh-kb-rag README · Model download (the usual blocker)：The first search downloads the two models (~1.2 GB). This is the step most likely to stall. Let the plugin fetch them, or pre-download to a directory you choose:

```powershell
[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("HF_HOME", "<cache-dir>", "User")

dsh-kb-rag README · new shell：$env:HF_HOME = "<cache-dir>"
python -c "from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer; SentenceTransformer('BAAI/bge-small-zh-v1.5')"
python -c "from sentence_transformers import CrossEncoder; CrossEncoder('BAAI/bge-reranker-base')"
```

dsh-kb-rag README · new shell：Install `sentence-transformers` first if Python reports it missing. `kb_stats` reports whether both models are cached. If the default download stalls, set `HF_ENDPOINT=https://hf-mirror.com` and `KB_HF_MIRROR_FIRST=1`, restart DSH, and retry. Full notes: [docs/MIGRATION-1.6.8.md](docs/MIGRATION-1.6.8.md#模型预下载可选).

Already on 1.6.7? The plugin panel checks the installed 1.6.7 manifest, so installing 1.6.8 can fail with an error that quotes 1.6.7. Uninstall 1.6.7 first, then install 1.6.8.

dsh-kb-rag README · B. Coming from DSH web：The web profile is not a supported install target. Install the DSH desktop app, then follow A. The knowledge base (`.kb`) stays where it is; only the plugin host changes. Remove the old web-profile copy so the two do not drift:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-kb-rag
```

dsh-kb-rag README · C. From source (maintainers)：```bash
git clone https://github.com/Breeze136/dsh-kb-rag.git && cd dsh-kb-rag
./npm-package/scripts/install.sh        # macOS / Linux / Git Bash

dsh-kb-rag README · Windows: install.cmd, or npm-package\scripts\install.ps1：```

If your desktop build cannot search npm, install [dsh-plugin-registry](https://github.com/beancookie/dsh-plugin-registry) once and use its marketplace panel. kb-rag is listed there.

> [!WARNING]
> Do not run `npm install dsh-kb-rag` inside a DSH profile. It writes an npm-style `node_modules` next to pnpm's symlink store, and later `dsh plugin` operations become unpredictable. `npm install` is only for a deployment you manage by hand; see [npm-package/README.md](npm-package/README.md).

dsh-kb-rag README · Troubleshooting：| Symptom | What it means | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Panel quotes `@1.6.7 ... incompatible` | It checks the installed 1.6.7 manifest | Uninstall 1.6.7, restart, install 1.6.8 |
| `Cannot find package ...\dsh-kb-rag\index.js` | The GitHub repo root was installed, not npm | Uninstall it, install `dsh-kb-rag` from npm |
| `.hotload\...\package.json` missing | Stale local-preview metadata | Reinstall 1.6.8; clear the panel cache if it persists |
| Install worked, no `kb_*` tools | Old session, or the profile still has 1.6.7 | Restart DSH, open a new conversation, check the version |
| `/kb` missing in a brand-new session | The command list has not refreshed yet | Send one message, then type `/kb`; the tools work without it |
| Missing Python packages or models | Engine dependencies, not the plugin | Run the command in the error, or set `KB_AUTO_PIP=1`; models use `HF_ENDPOINT` |
dsh-kb-rag README · Troubleshooting：Details and the before-report checklist: [docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md](docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md).

dsh-kb-rag README · Build a library：Three ways in, depending on where the paper lives right now:

**Zotero library (do this first).** Preview before syncing, so a whole library does not move in by accident:

> Show me which Zotero items with PDF attachments can be ingested, without running it yet.

dsh-kb-rag README · Build a library：That is `kb_zotero(dry_run=true)`. Drop `dry_run` to run it; add `async_mode=true` for a whole-library migration. Zotero's title, authors, year, journal and DOI are written into the search results; items without a local PDF attachment are skipped, and nothing is downloaded for you. If auto-detection fails, pass the `zotero.sqlite` path explicitly.

**A folder of PDFs.**

> Add this graphene literature folder to the knowledge base and tell me how many files were added, skipped and failed.

dsh-kb-rag README · Build a library：Pass the folder path along; the agent calls `kb_ingest`, which handles PDF, TXT, MD and DOCX. Unchanged files are skipped by SHA-256; identical copies are recognised by hash and not indexed twice; a file is only re-parsed when its content changes.

**A single paper.** Give `kb_fetch` a DOI or arXiv ID and it downloads and indexes in one step:

> Use kb_fetch to fetch 10.5555/12345678, then ingest it.

dsh-kb-rag README · Build a library：Above `KB_ASYNC_THRESHOLD` (default 25) pending files, the batch forks into a background job and returns a `job_id` immediately. Poll it with `kb_status` until it reports `done`; a host-side timeout does not interrupt the job.

**Prefer PDFs that have a text layer.** A scanned PDF has none, so parsing fails with `no text extracted`; the engine does not OCR. Run such files through an OCR tool first, then ingest the result.

dsh-kb-rag README · Ask：- "Which papers discuss graphene growth on copper?" → `kb_search`
- "Which page states this?" → the `page` field on the evidence, or the Zotero page link
- "Answer only from the library" → strict mode through `kb_scope` (DSH)

Two retrieval modes, `quick` by default:

dsh-kb-rag README · Ask：- **`quick` (default)** — find papers, look up terms, locate a passage fast. Hybrid recall, with no reranking, citation linking or related work.
- **`deep`** — compare methods across papers, build a review, follow a citation chain. Adds a reranker on top of hybrid recall, plus citation links and related work.

dsh-kb-rag README · Ask：**Start with `quick`.** Its job is to confirm the library is built and returns grounded passages (0.2-0.4 s warm); once that checks out, switch to `deep` (1-2 s warm) for cross-paper comparison or citation chains. Switch in the conversation, set a session default with `/kb deep`, or pass `depth: "deep"` in MCP.

dsh-kb-rag README · Ask：For a formatted answer, say "generate an HTML report": the agent passes an `answer` object and the engine writes a self-contained HTML page next to a gallery of earlier answers. Ten templates cover an instant one-screen card, a review, a method breakdown, a comparison, numeric findings, a timeline, a glossary, disputes, a derivation, and Q&A. See [HTML answers](#html-answers).

dsh-kb-rag README · Ask：

Figure 5　Three steps: build the library, ask in the chat, export a self-contained HTML answer. The index is built once.

dsh-kb-rag README · Ask：

Figure 6　Four of the ten answer templates: instant card, comparison, numeric KPIs, timeline.

dsh-kb-rag README · HTML answers：When a chat reply gets long and hard to scan, ask for an HTML report instead: in DSH, say "write this up as a shareable HTML report" and the agent passes an `answer` object to `kb_rag`. A plain `kb_rag` call returns evidence for the model to answer from and writes no file. The engine lays out the page itself: there is no model call, and rendering the sample pages takes 2-4 ms, separate from retrieval. The result's `answer_file` object carries `path`, `url`, `bytes`, `template`, `layout` and `warnings`.

dsh-kb-rag README · HTML answers： *Rendered `compare` answer in English. The localized chrome is a preview of the next release; 1.6.8 ships Chinese chrome.* [Open the live page](https://breeze136.github.io/dsh-kb-rag/demo/answer-en.html) ```jsonc { "query": "graphene CVD nucleation density on copper", "depth": "quick", "answer": {
dsh-kb-rag README · HTML answers：**Templates.** The template fixes the sections, their order and each block's renderer; fields it does not define are ignored, and empty ones are skipped.

dsh-kb-rag README · HTML answers：| `template` | Use it for | Main fields |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `instant` | one-screen answer to a single question | `answer`, `limit`, `followup` |
| `review` | synthesis across several papers | `bottom_line`, `state`, `methods`, `limits`, `takeaway` |
| `method` | one method end to end | `what`, `when`, `steps`, `params`, `figure`, `caveats` |
| `compare` | side-by-side comparison | `bottom_line`, `matrix`, `numbers`, `reading` |
| `numeric` | when the numbers are the point | `bottom_line`, `kpis`, `numbers`, `trend`, `reading` |
| `timeline` | how a line of work developed | `bottom_line`, `line` |
| `concept` | terms and definitions | `cards` |
| `dispute` | papers that disagree | `bottom_line`, `issues` |
| `derivation` | a derivation with a checkable result | `conventions`, `deriv`, `figure`, `result`, `code`, `verify`, `pitfalls` |
| `qa` | a concept explained in Q&A form | `intro`, `questions`, `summary` |

dsh-kb-rag README · HTML answers：`stage: "instant"` is a shortcut: it selects `instant`, sets a 300-character budget, and forces `quick`. `layout: "doc"` switches from the card layout to long-form. `summary` supplies a one-line lead when the template has no `bottom_line`, or that field is empty.

dsh-kb-rag README · HTML answers：**Fields.** A section takes a string, `{ text, refs }`, an array, a table (`{ columns: [{ label, num, heat, bar }], rows: [[...]] }` or a markdown pipe table), `{ items: [{ label, value, unit }] }` for `rank` and `kpis`, `{ x, series }` for `chart`, and `{ nodes, edges }` for `flow`. `refs` are 1-based indexes into this call's evidence; a number outside that range is reported in `warnings` and renders as a marker with no source. Write numbers and units as the paper gives them; the renderer derives axis ranges, ticks, bar lengths, heat levels and sort order, so do not pre-compute them. Fields are clipped at the template limit, and the whole envelope at `budget.max_total_chars` when set; every clip is listed in `warnings`.

dsh-kb-rag README · HTML answers：**Files.** Pages land in `~/.kb-rag/answers/` as `<date>_<question-slug>-<hash8>.html`, next to `index.html` (a gallery of the latest 200 answers, newest first) and `index.json`. Set `answer_dir` on the call (an absolute path, or one starting with `~`), or `KB_ANSWER_DIR` in the environment, to move the folder. The filename carries a content hash, so re-rendering the same envelope on the same day overwrites one file instead of adding another.

dsh-kb-rag README · HTML answers：**Open, print, share.** Open the file in any browser; it needs no server and no network. Formula pages are the one exception: they load MathJax from jsDelivr and fall back to raw TeX if that request fails. Two buttons at the top print or export to PDF and copy the body as Markdown; Ctrl/Cmd+P works too, and the layout holds down to phone width. The footer ends with the retrieval and render time for that answer:

```text
检索 1.6 s · 渲染 12 ms
```

dsh-kb-rag README · HTML answers：Text-only clients still get the compact card; the HTML file is an addition, not a dependency.

**Colours.** Four presets (blue, green, ink, warm) are switchable from a control at the bottom and are remembered in that browser. To pin a default for the workspace, create `.kb-rag/answer-theme.json` next to `.kb`; a `theme` object on the call overrides it.

dsh-kb-rag README · HTML answers：**Limits in 1.6.8.** The page chrome is Chinese; English chrome is planned for the next release. Unknown `template` names fall back to `review` in the engine; the DSH tool schema rejects them first.

dsh-kb-rag README · HTML answers：| Symptom | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| Text answer only, no file | `answer` was not passed; ask for a report explicitly |
| `answer_file.ok` is false | the error text names the cause; fix it and re-run |
| A section is missing | its field was empty; empty sections are omitted |
| A field ends in `…` | the field hit its limit; `warnings` says which one |
| A citation marker has no source | its `refs` number is outside this call's evidence; `warnings` names it |
| Chinese labels in an English report | The chrome is Chinese; the body text is unchanged |

dsh-kb-rag README · Tools：| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `kb_ingest` | Ingest files or folders (PDF/TXT/MD/DOCX). Incremental skip, deduplication, section chunking, vectorisation. `metadata_only=true` refreshes title/authors/year/journal/DOI in place; `rebuild=true` re-parses every indexed document; large batches move to a background job |
| `kb_status` | Poll a background job: progress while `running`, totals and recent files when `done`, or the error |
| `kb_zotero` | Migrate a local Zotero library, including PDF attachments |
| `kb_search` | Hybrid retrieval returning passages with title, authors, year, journal, DOI, page and section |
| `kb_rag` | Evidence-based answering with numbered citations; optional HTML answer page |
| `kb_scope` | Query scope (library / library plus web / web), strict mode, retrieval depth |
| `kb_dedup` | Remove duplicate documents, keeping the earliest copy |
| `kb_clear` | Wipe all documents and indexes; requires `confirm=true` |
| `kb_stats` | Document, chunk and vector counts, recent ingests, model cache state, stale documents |
| `kb_fetch` | Download a PDF by DOI or arXiv ID (publisher version first, open-access fallback) |

dsh-kb-rag README · Tools：The MCP server exposes 10 tools as well, including `kb_status` and a diagnostic `kb_mcp_status`. `kb_scope` is DSH-specific and has no MCP equivalent. MCP keeps `kb_rag`'s default at `deep`; the DSH plugin defaults to `quick`. Configuration and client snippets: [mcp-server/README.md](mcp-server/README.md).

dsh-kb-rag README · Engine capabilities：- Chunking is section-aware: abstracts get weight 1.5, methods 1.2. It also handles inline headings, abstract promotion, caption blocks and paragraph merging for non-article documents.
- Retrieval combines BM25 (with CJK bigrams), bge-small vector cosine, RRF fusion and section weights.
- Reranking uses bge-reranker-base to cut the top 20 down to 3, with a bge-large-en bi-encoder as fallback.
- Every passage carries its PDF page and section. The page renders as `section · p.N` and maps onto Zotero's `?page=N` link.
- In-text `[n]` markers resolve to reference entries. Nature-style superscripts are detected from font metrics, so `graphene1,2` becomes `graphene[1,2]`. Cited works are matched by DOI, normalised title, or first author plus year, and in-library matches are marked.
- SHA-256 hashes skip unchanged files (about 40× faster on re-runs) and catch duplicate copies across folders.
- Each document records the parser revision that wrote it (`docs.indexed_with`), so `kb_stats` can report rows an older revision left behind.
- Identical queries hit a cache. Any ingest or engine rebuild clears it.
- The engine runs as a resident daemon. Models

dsh-kb-rag README · Query guidance：Ask in whatever language you think in. The agent rewrites your question into an English term string before it reaches the engine — most libraries are around 98% English — and adds a query in your own words when you want documents in that language.

Two things are worth doing:

dsh-kb-rag README · Query guidance：- **Ask one thing at a time**, naming the material, method and property together. That retrieves far better than "summarise this for me".
- **Say the limits out loud** — "only papers from 2020 on", "just this journal". The agent turns them into `filters` rather than stuffing them into the query.

The mechanics — why a CJK keyword query cannot match English body text, which fields `filters` supports, what `lang_note` means — are in [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md), section 5.

dsh-kb-rag README · MCP：```bash
pip install -r mcp-server/requirements.txt
python mcp-server/server.py
```

Register it as a stdio server in Claude Desktop, Cherry Studio, Kimi, Cursor, DeepSeek or another MCP host. The server shares the same engine and the same `kb.sqlite`. By default it uses `~/.kb-rag` rather than the DSH workspace `.kb`, and every tool accepts `kb_root` to point elsewhere. See [mcp-server/README.md](mcp-server/README.md) for config snippets, capability quarantine and timeout behaviour.

dsh-kb-rag README · Architecture：```text
DSH model / MCP client (Claude, Cherry, Kimi, Cursor, ...)
   |  tool call: kb_ingest / kb_search / kb_rag / kb_stats ...
   v
plugin host (JS) or MCP server (server.py + engine_client.py)
dsh-kb-rag README · Measured performance：Windows, CPU inference unless noted. Query numbers come from a 248-document / 20,760-chunk library; ingest numbers from a 242-file / 1.8 GB run.

dsh-kb-rag README · Measured performance：| Metric | Result |
|---|---|
| Query latency (warm) | `quick` 0.33-0.38 s; `deep` 1.4-1.9 s, median 1.6 s |
| Cold first call | up to 8.9 s while models load |
| Ingest throughput | 242 PDF/DOCX files (1.8 GB) in 85.9 s, about 355 ms per document |
| Incremental re-run | same directory in 2.17 s, a 40× speed-up |
| HTML answer render | 2-4 ms per page in the sample set; retrieval is timed separately |
| Full re-index (GPU) | 316 PDFs / 23.5k chunks / 20.1k vectors in 219 s on an 8 GB consumer GPU, zero errors |
| Embedding throughput | 164 chunks/s on GPU vs 37 chunks/s on CPU (~4.4×); flat from batch 32 to 256, so tokenisation is the limiting factor |
dsh-kb-rag README · Measured performance：Methodology and design rationale: [`docs/DESIGN.md`](docs/DESIGN.md).
dsh-kb-rag README · Device handling (GPU / CPU)：Ingestion and search share one embedding model. A CUDA build of torch is used automatically (`KB_DEVICE=auto`, the default).

dsh-kb-rag README · Device handling (GPU / CPU)：- The device is probed before the first model load with a tiny matmul. A driver can report a GPU and still fail at the first kernel, so the probe catches that early and falls back to CPU with a readable reason. `KB_GPU_PROBE=0` skips the probe.
- Device failures during a call degrade instead of aborting: the batch is halved, then cut to 4, then the model moves to CPU and the call finishes. The batch size that worked is remembered. Non-device errors are raised unchanged.
- `reload` resets the device verdict after a driver fix. `drop_models=true` reloads the models onto the GPU without restarting the host.
- Batch sizes follow the device and free VRAM. `KB_EMBED_BATCH` / `KB_RERANK_BATCH` override them, but raising them does not speed up small models.
- CPU-only is about 4× slower on the embedding step. PDF extraction, chunking and BM25 are CPU-bound either way.
dsh-kb-rag README · Device handling (GPU / CPU)：`kb_stats` reports the outcome in `device`, including `gpu_disabled_reason` and `note` when a fallback happened.

| `KB_DEVICE` | `auto` | Engine | `auto` uses a working CUDA device; `cpu` / `cuda` / `cuda:1` / `mps` force a choice. Device failures fall back to CPU |

dsh-kb-rag README · Configuration：A workspace file `.kb-rag/engine.env` (KEY=VALUE, one per line) is merged into the engine's environment at startup; explicit environment variables win. It is the practical way to pin a model or mirror per library without editing system settings.

dsh-kb-rag README · Repository layout：```text
kb-rag/
├─ kb_engine.py              Python engine: chunking, retrieval, reranking, serve daemon
├─ install.cmd               Windows entry point (runs scripts\install.ps1)
├─ scripts/                  Installer scripts (install.ps1, install.sh)

Runtime data: the DSH plugin writes to `.kb/kb.sqlite` in the session workspace; the MCP server defaults to `~/.kb-rag/kb.sqlite`. Background job files live in `<kb_root>/.kb-jobs/` and are removed when a job finishes.

dsh-kb-rag README · Known limitations：- Scanned PDFs are not supported. Documents without a text layer are skipped; OCR is out of scope.
- Page anchors are PDF-only. TXT, MD and DOCX files, and documents indexed before schema v3, fall back to section-level location until re-ingested with `force`.
- Citation linking requires a re-ingest. Superscript detection and reference splitting run at parse time.
- Metadata is only as good as the PDF. It is never 100% accurate; when it is missing, title and year are judged from the cover page, and existing Zotero metadata is preferred.
- Captions are searchable as text; content that exists only inside a figure is not.
- Keyword matching is in memory. Beyond a few hundred thousand chunks, FAISS HNSW or SQLite FTS5 would be the next step.
- Some publishers redirect automated PDF requests to a login page. `kb_fetch` reports the failure and leaves the manual path (download, then `kb_ingest`) as the fallback.
